rows.what: Management › Tasks lists every task on the project, whatever raised it — the tab's dialog, a milestone, AI, compliance, a floor-plan mark, an approval or the rail's Tasks page.
rows.v2: Project › Tasks › All tasks

rows.what: The tab reads “Management (N)”: every open task the viewer may see, approval and compliance tasks included.
rows.v2: Project › tab strip › Tasks badge
rows.how: The badge counts what waits on you there — overdue plus due today — not every open task.

rows.what: Tasks sit in Not Started · In Progress · Completed cards with filter chips and counts, collapse per card, and move between statuses (Move to).
rows.how: A task is open or done; the Filters' Status pane picks open or completed.

rows.what: A grid of Title · Type · Milestone · Owner · Due · Actions; pressing a head sorts every card, Due first by default.
rows.v2: Project › Tasks › All tasks (table, Column settings, Filters › Sort)
rows.how: Columns are Title · Milestone · Members · Creator · Due · Status · Tags, reordered or hidden in Column settings; sorting is Due · Newest · Oldest in Filters, not by pressing a column head.

rows.what: A task shows its milestone as a pill and picks one in Add / Edit — but the tab and the milestone use two different links, so counts disagree and a change made on edit is lost.
rows.v2: Project › Tasks › Milestone column; task panel › Milestone; Filters › Milestone

rows.what: Fifteen task types shown as coloured pills (Quote Approval, VO Approval, Member Invite, Project Closure, General…); tasks made in the tab are always General.
rows.v2: Task panel › kind
rows.how: Three kinds — General, Call, Follow-up. The approval types are no longer tasks (TD-012).

rows.what: One shown owner — any studio member (not just the team), an outside person “(Ext)” or the homeowner; “Unassigned” cannot be saved and the first member in the list is the default.
rows.v1: Project › Management › Tasks › Owner; Add Task › Assign to
rows.v2: Project › Tasks › Members column; task panel › Members
rows.how: Several members per task, from the people the viewer may assign; a task may have no one; an outside person sits beside the members (TD-018); never the client (TD-020).

rows.what: Each task has a due date, shown in red once it has passed while the task is open.
rows.v2: Project › Tasks › Due column; task panel › Due date and time

rows.what: A tick completes a task; on a completed task an ✕ moves it back to Not Started.
rows.v2: Project › Tasks › row tick (with Undo)

rows.what: A hover-only ⋯ (unreachable on touch) with Edit task · Move to a status · Delete task.
rows.v2: Project › Tasks › row ⋮
rows.how: The menu holds Mark as completed · Rename · Save as template · Duplicate · Send on WhatsApp (outside person) · Delete; there is no Move to a status.

rows.what: Delete task quietly sets the task to Cancelled, with no confirmation; it disappears and can never be seen or restored.
rows.v1: Project › Management › Tasks › row ⋯ › Delete task
rows.v2: Project › Tasks › row ⋮ › Delete
rows.how: Delete asks first (“This action cannot be undone”), then removes the task for good; Activity keeps a line naming it.

rows.what: Approvals (quote, timeline, milestone, stage, VO, expense, PO, commission, invoice, closure) arrive as tasks with Approve / Reject and a reason, plus shortcuts such as Revise Timeline and View Project on the rail page.
rows.v2: The record's own review (quote approval bar, update review, invoice approval, schedule asks) + a bell row + the Overview's Needs you
rows.how: An approval is a state on its own record with a bell row and a Needs you row, checked on the server — not a task.

rows.feature: Select tasks and act on them
rows.what: Tick rows inside one status card, then Move to another status for all of them; no select-all.
rows.v2: Project › Tasks › tick rows › bulk bar
rows.how: The bulk bar offers Assign · Mark as completed · Save as template · Duplicate · Delete (Delete All when every task is ticked), with Undo on complete and assign; no status move.

rows.what: A dialog with title, milestone, assignee, due date and status (the chosen status is ignored; new tasks always start Not Started).
rows.v1: Project › Management › Tasks › Add Task / row click
rows.v2: Project › Create strip › Task, or the list's add row; the task's side panel
rows.how: A task is added by its title in the list, then edited in a side panel — title, description, due date and time, members, tags, files, milestone, outside person — each change saved as it is made.

rows.feature: Description and pictures on a task
rows.what: A task can carry a description and up to five pictures (5 MB each), but only the milestone's dialog edits them; the tab shows icons only.
rows.v2: Task panel › Description · Attach files
rows.how: Every task's panel edits the description and attaches files — picked from the project's Files or uploaded, pictures or any other file.

rows.what: A member who is only a designer sees just the tasks assigned to them, everywhere — not even ones they gave to an outside person — so counts differ by viewer.
rows.v2: Who sees leads; Tasks (rail) › All Tasks · My Tasks · Unassigned · Studio Tasks
rows.how: Whoever may open the project sees all its tasks; narrowing to one's own is a scope on the rail's Tasks page.

rows.what: The assignee (and assigner) are told a task is assigned, and a reminder is queued for 30 minutes before the due time on the studio's chosen channels; both link to the rail's Tasks page.
rows.v2: Bell › A task is assigned to you · A task is due in 30 minutes (Settings › Notifications)
rows.how: The bell rows are real and open the task; the due reminder is worked out when the bell is read. Sending either by email or WhatsApp at the right moment needs the delivery adapter and a scheduled sweep that developers add.

rows.feature: Someone outside the studio on a task
rows.what: A task can go to a named person outside the studio (name and an optional phone), shown as “(Ext)”; no notice reaches them.
rows.v1: Milestone › View / Edit Tasks › Assign to › + Add person not in your studio
rows.v2: Task panel › Outside the studio; row ⋮ › Send on WhatsApp
rows.how: A subcontractor or supplier with a Singapore mobile (required), beside or instead of members, on any task; Send on WhatsApp drafts the task to them and records the send; filters, search and export know them.

rows.feature: Ask the Owner to invite an outside person
rows.what: “Request invite” on an outside person also raises a Member Invite task for the studio owner with the name and phone filled in.
rows.v1: Add a person not in your studio › Request invite
rows.how: The outside-person form has no invite request; an Owner or Admin adds members on Company › Members.

rows.what: A task can be assigned to the project's homeowner, meant for the portal's “Your to-dos” (behind a studio switch that is off by default).
rows.v1: Milestone › View / Edit Tasks › Assign to › Homeowner
rows.how: The client's asks are choices to make and stages to confirm.

rows.what: View / Edit Tasks for a milestone: a batch list with done ticks, per-row assignee, due date, description and pictures, an overdue count, all saved at once (saving reset In-progress tasks and revived deleted ones).
rows.v1: Project › Management › Milestones › milestone ⋯ › View / Edit Tasks
rows.v2: Project › Schedule › milestone panel › Tasks
rows.how: Each task opens in its row and saves as it changes (due date and time, members, description, outside person, Open in Tasks); new tasks are added by name; nothing is batch-saved.

rows.feature: AI task suggestions from the quote
rows.what: “Suggest from quote” asks an AI model for 5–8 tasks for the milestone and adds them unticked; when the AI fails it silently adds canned tasks.
rows.v1: Milestone › View / Edit Tasks › Suggest from quote
rows.how: Maison AI on a project proposes one next-step task from the project's records; task templates add sets of tasks.

rows.what: A milestone action replaces its tasks with AI ones; for a non-owner with milestone approval on, it raises “Approve tasks for: …” for the owner.
rows.how: No AI-made task sets, so no approval step for them.

rows.what: The rail's Tasks page filters by source — all, leads or projects.
rows.v2: Tasks (rail) › All · Leads · Projects

rows.what: Tasks group under each project (on by default), each header with open / active / done counts and Go to project.
rows.v2: Tasks (rail) › ⋮ › Group by project
rows.how: Each header reads “P-… · name · n tasks · Go to project”, then Leads, then Studio tasks; on by itself only for Projects; no per-status counts.

rows.what: Each row on the rail's Tasks page names its lead or project.
rows.v2: Tasks (rail) › For column

rows.feature: Add a task to a project from the Tasks page
rows.what: The rail's create dialog offers “Link to Project”.
rows.v1: Tasks (rail) › New task › Link to Project
rows.v2: Tasks (rail) › add row › Lead picker
rows.how: A Won lead can be picked (its tasks are its project's), but a project made with New project (no lead) is not offered — its tasks are added from the project's own Tasks.

rows.what: Management › Materials: cards of things for the homeowner to choose (category, title, options, price range, status, the pick, their comment), newest first, with empty and loading states.
rows.v2: Project › Design › Choices
rows.how: Called Choices, a view of the Design tab; grouped by room or by milestone; notices about an answer open the choice itself (1.0's opened Milestones).

rows.what: A required category picked from eight rooms (Kitchen, Master Bedroom, Living Room, Bathroom, Dining, Study, Balcony, Others).
rows.v2: Add a choice › Room or area · Milestone · Needed by
rows.how: Room or area is free text and optional; a choice can belong to a milestone and carry a needed-by date that flags it late.

rows.what: Up to four options, each with name, vendor / brand, price, image (pasted URL or upload), description and a separate “VO impact”.
rows.v2: Choice card › Add an option ▾; the option dialog
rows.how: Up to eight options, reorderable; name, a line, vendor and one price against the quote (adds · saves · no change — the VO impact); the picture comes from a source or an upload, never a pasted URL; no separate display price.

rows.feature: Pick an option from the catalogue
rows.what: “Choose from catalog” searches the studio's material catalog and copies an item into the option.
rows.v1: New Selection › option › Choose from catalog
rows.v2: Add an option ▾ › From Materials · From the Price book · From a render · Upload a picture
rows.how: Four sources instead of one: Company › Materials, the Price book, a render from the AI Visualizer, an upload.

rows.feature: Save an option to the catalogue
rows.what: “Save” on an option adds it to the studio's material catalog, filed under the selection's category.
rows.v2: Option ⋮ › Save to Materials… · Save to the Price book…
rows.how: Offered for uploaded and render options; a Designer's Price book item goes in as a proposal; the option then names its new source.

rows.feature: A note for the team only
rows.what: A designer note on a selection that only the team sees, never sent to the homeowner.
rows.v2: Edit choice › A note for the team

rows.feature: Save and share with the client
rows.what: Save as Draft or Save & Share with Client in the dialog; Share with Client on a Draft card, with no confirmation or message.
rows.v1: New Selection footer; card ⋮ › Share with Client
rows.v2: Choice card ⋮ › Share with {client} · Take back
rows.how: Add choice saves a draft; sharing is its own step from the card, with Undo, and a choice waiting on the client can be taken back to Draft.

rows.feature: The client is told about a shared choice
rows.what: Only an older, unused route notified the homeowner; sharing from the board told them nothing.
rows.v2: The client's portal bell; Settings › Notifications › Messages to clients › A choice to make
rows.how: Sharing rings the client's portal bell and sends “A choice to make” by email or WhatsApp through the delivery layer — a stand-in the developers wire; Sent messages logs it.

rows.what: Draft → Shared → Approved / Change Requested / Rejected; after a no the studio can edit the options but can never share it again.
rows.v2: Choice card chip and band
rows.how: Draft · Shared · Chosen · Declined — the client either asks for other options or turns them down, with a reason; the card's band offers Share again or Choose with {client}.

rows.feature: The studio hears the client's answer
rows.what: Any answer sends the studio a notice with the selection, the option picked and the comment (its link opened Milestones).
rows.v2: Bell › A client makes a choice · A client says no to a choice

rows.what: The pick is stored as a position in the list; an approved selection can still be edited, so the shown pick can drift to another option.
rows.v2: Choice card › Chosen; ⋮ › Change the pick
rows.how: The pick is kept by the option itself; a chosen choice's options are locked; the studio can change the pick with the client until the work it belongs to starts.

rows.what: The card shows the lowest and highest option price.
rows.v2: Choice card › each option's price
rows.how: Each option says what it does to the quote — +S$… · −S$… · No change — and notes GST when the project charges it.

rows.feature: A priced pick drafts a variation order
rows.what: Approving an option with a VO impact drafts a variation order and notifies the studio; the card's link to it opens the wrong place.
rows.v2: Choice card › its variation order; Money › variation orders

rows.what: Delete asks “This action cannot be undone” and removes the selection in any status.
rows.v2: Choice card ⋮ › Delete
rows.how: Delete has Undo and is refused once chosen — the choice stays as the record of the pick.

rows.what: Any signed-in member can create, edit, share and delete selections, on any project, locked or not.
rows.v2: Project › Design › Choices (its rules)
rows.how: The project's team, their Managers, Owners and Admins change choices; others read; a completed project's choices are read-only.

rows.what: Accounts › Material Catalog keeps reusable materials (name, vendor, price, image, specs) that options are picked from and saved to.
rows.v2: Company › Materials (and the Price book)
rows.how: Company › Materials — the AI Visualizer's library — is the place; the Price book is a second source for options.

rows.feature: A receipt of the client's decision
rows.what: A PDF decision receipt for every answered selection — options with prices, ✓ on the pick, the status (approved, rejected or change requested), the comment, a document hash — made on download.
rows.v2: Choice card ⋮ › Selection receipt
rows.how: A printable page (Download PDF prints it) with a fingerprint, for every confirmed pick and re-issued when the pick changes; a client's no gets no receipt.

rows.what: Files & Docs shows up to twelve answered selections as tiles that download the receipt (the count shows the cut number).
rows.v2: Project › Files & notes › Files › Choices
rows.how: Each receipt is an entry in Files › Choices that opens its page; nothing is cut at twelve.

rows.feature: A shared floor plan on the project
rows.what: Management › Floor Plan: a plan the studio and the homeowner both mark up and discuss, with loading and error states.
rows.v2: Project › Design › Floor plan
rows.how: A view of the Design tab; the client's side is the portal's own Floor plan section, with its own switch.

rows.what: Upload a PNG, JPEG, WebP or PDF (a PDF's first page is drawn at 2,400 px and the original kept); limits 5 MB for a picture, 20 MB for a PDF.
rows.v1: Floor Plan › Upload plan / Upload another plan
rows.v2: Floor plan › Add a plan (+)
rows.how: One 8 MB limit; the original is a file in Files › Floor plans, opened from ⋮ › Open the original.

rows.feature: Use a file already on the project
rows.what: “Or import from a file already attached” lists the project's and lead's pictures, each with Use as plan.
rows.v1: Floor Plan › first run › import list
rows.v2: Add a plan › From the project's Files; ⋮ › Use a file from Files

rows.feature: Ask the client for the plan
rows.what: “Don't have it? Ask your homeowner to send it” emails the homeowner a request.
rows.v1: Floor Plan › first run › Ask your homeowner
rows.v2: Floor plan first run › Invite {client} to the portal; the client's portal › Send the plan
rows.how: No request message: the studio can invite a client who is not on the portal, where an empty Floor plan offers Send the plan, but cannot ask a client already on it.

rows.what: A switcher of plan cards (thumbnail, uploader, mark count, ★ Primary) with Set as Primary, Rename and Archive; every studio upload silently becomes Primary and emails the homeowner again.
rows.v2: Floor plan › plan chips; ⋮ › Make it the main plan · Rename · Put away · Plans put away
rows.how: “Main plan”; adding a plan asks whether it becomes the main one; plans are chips (no thumbnail, uploader or mark count); Put away has Undo and a list to bring plans back.

rows.what: Pen, Box, Arrow, Text, numbered comment pins, photo pins, three hatched zones, revision clouds and numbered callouts, each mark saved the moment it is drawn.
rows.v2: Floor plan › toolbar

rows.what: Ten stamps: single and double 13A sockets, light switch, data / TV point, aircon point, downlight, cove light, pendant, water point, floor trap.
rows.v2: Floor plan › toolbar › Stamp

rows.what: A style popover with colour (the role's colour by default), thickness and dashed lines.
rows.v2: Floor plan › toolbar › colour and weight

rows.what: Wheel, pinch and ± zoom from 100% to 800%, a Pan mode, and double-click or Fit to width to reset.
rows.v2: Floor plan › canvas zoom bar

rows.feature: Select, move, erase and undo marks
rows.what: Select a mark to open its thread, drag your own marks to move them, erase your own, and ⌘Z removes your last mark.
rows.v2: Floor plan › Select · Erase · Undo (⌘Z, Enter, Esc)

rows.feature: Plan scale and measuring in millimetres
rows.what: Teach the plan one known length (two clicks, then the size), after which Measure reads real millimetres.
rows.v2: Floor plan › Scale · Measure

rows.what: Eight trade layers with show / hide and counts; marks on Studio only are removed from the homeowner's data on the server.
rows.v2: Floor plan › Layer menu; the rail's layer chips

rows.what: Both · Studio · Homeowner pills, a hide-resolved toggle and a count, with empty states when a filter hides everything.
rows.v2: Floor plan › rail › Both · Studio · {client}; Show resolved marks

rows.what: Each mark has a thread with photos (up to five per comment, photos alone allowed), Studio / Homeowner pills, Mark resolved / Reopen, and an instant, permanent delete of your own marks.
rows.v2: Floor plan › mark card
rows.how: Deleting a mark is soft, with Undo; the client is named rather than “Homeowner”.

rows.feature: Turn a mark into a task
rows.what: Make a task creates a General task for whoever pressed it — no due date, no milestone, no notice; a second press is refused.
rows.v1: Floor Plan › mark card › Make a task
rows.v2: Floor plan › mark card › Make a task
rows.how: The task is assigned (the bell rings), linked to the mark, opens from the snackbar on Tasks, and a second press opens the same task.

rows.feature: Turn a mark into a variation order
rows.what: Raise a variation order opens the VO editor and links the saved order to the mark.
rows.v1: Floor Plan › mark card › Raise a variation order
rows.v2: Floor plan › mark card › Raise a variation order
rows.how: Only for those who may change money; it drafts VO-n named after the project and opens the quote editor with Back to the plan.

rows.feature: The client's layout sign-off, seen by the studio
rows.what: A banner: “Layout confirmed by {name} · date” (confirmed in the portal, not a contract-grade signature), a warning when viewing another plan, or “Waiting on your homeowner”.
rows.v2: Floor plan › banner

rows.what: Stamps counted per symbol under their groups, honouring the author filter.
rows.v2: Floor plan › rail › Points

rows.what: Photo pins grouped by the day the photos were taken, with thumbnails.
rows.v2: Floor plan › rail › Site diary

rows.feature: Export the marked plan for the contractor
rows.what: Export marked plan (PDF): two A4 landscape pages — the plan with its marks and a numbered legend — made in the browser and named after the plan, not the project.
rows.v2: Floor plan › Download PDF for the contractor
rows.how: A print page (the browser makes the PDF) under the project's name, with the points counted and an Include Studio only switch.

rows.feature: The studio hears the client's marks
rows.what: The studio is told of the homeowner's marks, comments and uploads — at most once per plan every 15 minutes — and of a confirmed layout.
rows.v2: Bell › A client marks up the floor plan · A client confirms a layout

rows.feature: The client is told of a new plan
rows.what: Every studio upload emails the homeowner a link to the plan.
rows.v2: The client's portal bell › A floor plan from your designer
rows.how: Only the client's portal bell says so; no email or WhatsApp goes out for a new plan.

rows.what: The floor plan refetches every 8 seconds so both sides see new marks.
rows.how: It refreshes after each write and when the page comes back into view.

rows.feature: Preview the plan as the client
rows.what: The studio previewing as the homeowner sees the plan read-only, without tools.
rows.v2: Invite to Portal › See it as {client}
rows.how: The preview is the client's real portal opened read-only from the Invite to Portal panel.

rows.feature: Who may change the floor plan
rows.what: Studio-only powers exist only because their routes are studio routes; any member can add, mark and archive, even on a locked project.
rows.v2: Project › Design › Floor plan (its rules)
rows.how: Drawing, comments, main plan, rename, put away and scale belong to the team, their Managers, Owners and Admins; a completed project's floor plan is read-only.

rows.feature: Plan the Space (3D) from a project
rows.what: A header button opens a dialog listing up to five of the project's layouts or Start a new 3D layout, then the separate planner — but a layout is never saved with the project, so the list stays empty and Back leaves the project.
rows.v2: Project › Create strip › 3-D Space Planner (phone: ⋮ › Create); Design › Designs
rows.how: The dialog lists every layout of the project; a layout is saved with the project when made, names it in the editor's bar, and Back returns to the project.

rows.what: 3-D Space Planner page: My Floor Plans, a start area (Create New, Generate with AI, Upload image), Quick Start Templates and Custom Templates.
rows.v2: Tools › 3-D Space Planner
rows.how: A gallery of layouts with a Kind filter (Projects · Personal), search, a list view, rename / duplicate / delete with Undo and Deleted Layouts; New ▾ From a flat template · For a project · Blank.

rows.what: “Made with Space Planner”: showcase layouts that open as starting points.
rows.v1: Tools › 3-D Space Planner › Made with Space Planner
rows.how: No showcase of sample layouts; the six flat templates are the starting points.

rows.what: Quick Start Templates filtered All · HDB · Condo · Landed · Multi-Floor · Pre-Furnished (HDB 3-Room, 3-Room + Balcony, 4-Room, 5-Room, Condo 2- and 3-Bedroom, Landed House).
rows.v1: Tools › 3-D Space Planner › Quick Start Templates
rows.v2: New layout › flat cards (All · HDB · Condo · Landed) · Start with furniture placed
rows.how: Six flats (no 3-Room + Balcony); Pre-Furnished became the Start with furniture placed switch; no Multi-Floor filter.

rows.what: The room creator and templates allow several floors in one plan.
rows.how: One level per layout; a second storey is a second layout.

rows.what: Save as Template keeps a layout as a starting point (stored in the browser only).
rows.v1: 3-D Space Planner › Save › Save as Template
rows.how: Duplicate is the way to reuse a layout.

rows.feature: Draw rooms, walls, doors and windows
rows.what: Draw rooms from scratch with presets, and edit walls, doors (single, double, sliding, pocket, bifold, opening) and windows.
rows.v1: 3-D Space Planner › Create New Floor Plan · Edit Rooms
rows.v2: Layout editor › Rooms panel; Top view
rows.how: Rectangular rooms from ten presets or drawn on the Top view, each side a wall or open; one kind of door (a wide one draws as sliding panels).

rows.what: Upload a floor-plan image and AI turns it into rooms, with a guided wizard to fix what it misread.
rows.v2: New layout › Trace the floor plan
rows.how: No AI reading: the project's floor plan lies under the Top view at its true scale and the studio draws the rooms over it.

rows.what: Upload a room photo and AI makes a furnished 3D room.
rows.how: The AI Visualizer works on room photos instead.

rows.what: Dollhouse (3D), Cutaway, Top View and Walk (first person).
rows.v2: Layout editor › Top · 3D · Walk; Walls Full · Low
rows.how: Dollhouse and Cutaway are one 3D view with Walls Full or Low.

rows.what: Toolbar toggles Walls · Dims · Ruler · 2D · Furniture.
rows.v2: Layout editor › Walls Full · Low; dimensions on the Top view
rows.how: No Ruler to measure between two points, and no switch to hide the furniture or the dimensions (always drawn on the Top view).

rows.what: A catalogue (47 items in 9 categories in the docs; about 390 in its data file) with click-to-place and a ghost preview.
rows.v2: Layout editor › Furniture panel
rows.how: 42 simple parametric pieces in seven groups; press to place, or drag in on a desktop.

rows.what: Drag, rotate, resize, duplicate and delete pieces, with a 25 cm grid, 15 cm wall snap and collision checks that refuse a drop.
rows.v2: Layout editor › Top view / 3D; inspector
rows.how: A 5 cm grid with the same 15 cm wall snap; overlaps are outlined and named, not refused; one piece selected at a time.

rows.what: Each room gets a floor and wall colour or texture from eight presets.
rows.v2: Layout editor › Finishes panel
rows.how: Floors and walls take a material from the AI Visualizer's catalogue or Company › Materials.

rows.what: Delete, copy / paste / duplicate, undo / redo, arrows to nudge, select all, ⌘S to save, Esc, and ? for a shortcut list.
rows.v2: Layout editor keys; the ? shortcuts panel
rows.how: No select-all and no ⌘S (it saves itself); the shortcut list is the app's own ? panel.

rows.what: Manual Save (the first save creates the record), a local copy every 60 seconds for crash recovery, and a warning when leaving unsaved.
rows.v2: Layout editor (Saving… · Saved)
rows.how: The layout saves itself after each change and refuses a stale save, so nothing is lost; Undo / redo covers the visit.

rows.what: Each save stores a version with an automatic summary (“Added 2 items, Moved 1 item”), listed behind a count.
rows.how: The shared snapshot is the client's copy; Undo covers a visit.

rows.what: AI arranges the furniture in the rooms.
rows.how: “Start with furniture placed” furnishes a template's rooms by rule.

rows.feature: AI room render and render tour
rows.what: A photoreal render of the 3D scene, and a tour of several renders.
rows.v1: 3-D Space Planner › Render · Export › Render Tour
rows.how: The AI Visualizer renders rooms.

rows.what: Create a 3D piece from a text description, a photo or a catalogue page.
rows.v1: 3-D Space Planner › Create Furniture from Text / Photo / catalogue

rows.what: Room, Kitchen and Wardrobe elevation drawings.
Presentation mode, HD mode, faded or solid walls, and sun angle and time-of-day sliders.
rows.how: Walls Low stands in for faded walls.

rows.what: Export the layout as a PNG or a PDF.
rows.v2: Layout editor ⋮ › Download PNG · Download PDF
rows.how: The PDF is a print page: the plan under the project's name with a scale bar, a 3D view, the room schedule and the furniture list.

rows.v2: Layout editor › Share with client; ⋮ › Stop sharing
rows.how: The link holds a snapshot (later edits wait for Share changes); Copy or a WhatsApp draft; Stop sharing has Undo; a project's layout also reaches the client's portal.

rows.what: A public page with room pills that fly the camera, Orbit / Walk and fullscreen; phones and portrait screens are told to rotate.
rows.v2: /space/[token]
rows.how: 3D · Walk · Top with room chips, laid out for a phone too.

notes: 1.0 code with no screen was not given rows: the material-tracking API (F-169), the older selection routes (F-168), the hidden `?tab=render` Visualizer tab (H-207), the Gantt's unused compliance calculation (F-293) and the `tools/floorplan-3d-sandbox` calibration bench; the compliance checklist is mapped although 1.0 mounted it nowhere (F-272). The 3D planner's 6,875-line editor and its AI routes were checked through the inventory, `FloorPlanToolbar.tsx` and the entry page only, so planner rows describe the toolbar's features, not every behaviour. Inventory 26's row “Delete a task (asks; Undo)” is wrong: 2.0 asks, then deletes for good with no Undo (TD-011). Many “held” rows rest on the gaps-build packages' own calls (J-Q…, G-Q…, I-Q…), made “as recommended” under the owner's “build everything”, not on a call she made line by line. The rows marked missing are all low-severity extras (an invite request for an outside person, a planner showcase, Navigator notes, posting a render to Messages).
